issues.legal_issue: A legislature may retrospectively amend the definition underlying a house-tax levy to remove the basis of a prior judgment, and a tax confined to buildings occupied by a factory falls within the State’s taxing competence over lands and buildings.
material_facts: The local body levied house tax on factory and other buildings under a law authorizing house tax.
The earlier definition excluded the buildings because of their entrances and did not expressly include factories.
A later amendment retrospectively removed the entrance condition and expressly included factories, and the buildings fell within the amended definition.
The tax was imposed on the buildings, excluding machinery and furniture.
issues.conclusion: The retrospective amendment was valid because it changed the law and removed the basis of the earlier judgment rather than directing the State’s instrumentalities to disregard that judgment. The house tax was lawful, including as applied to the buildings occupied by the factory.
issues.legal_principle: Within its legislative competence and subject to constitutional limitations, a legislature may legislate retrospectively and may validate a levy by changing the law and removing the basis of a judicial decision. Article 246(3) read with Entry 49 of List II gives the State Legislature exclusive competence over taxes on lands and buildings; section 69(1)(a) authorized the local body to levy house tax, and Rule 6 excluded machinery and furniture from assessment. The Court applied United Provinces v. Atiqa Begum and Tirath Ram Rajindra Nath v. State of U.P.; it distinguished Municipal Corporation of the City of Allahabad v. New Shrock Spg. & Wvg. Co. Ltd., Janpada Sabha Chhindwara v. Central Provinces Syndicate Ltd., and State of Tamil Nadu v. M. Rayappa Gounder, where the legislative measures did not remove the basis of the judicial decisions or otherwise attempted to override them.

rule.if: civil_tax_appeal and retrospective_definition_amended and amended_definition_covers_assessed_buildings and local_law_authorizes_house_tax and tax_confined_to_buildings

predicates.civil_tax_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning the validity of a local body’s tax levy.
predicates.retrospective_definition_amended: The legislature changed the definition relevant to the tax and made that change apply to an earlier period.
predicates.amended_definition_covers_assessed_build: The buildings assessed fall within the changed definition.
predicates.local_law_authorizes_house_tax: The governing law authorizes the local body to impose house tax.
predicates.tax_confined_to_buildings: The tax is imposed on buildings and does not include machinery or furniture.

issues.definition: When a tax appeal concerns a tax authorized by law and confined to buildings covered by a retrospective change in definition, the house-tax levy is valid.

issues.legal_issue: A budget objection that was not raised below and requires factual investigation cannot be entertained for the first time on appeal.
material_facts: The contention that the local body could not impose taxes without a proper budget was not raised in the High Court.
Determining whether a budget had been prepared would require investigation of facts.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the budget objection.
issues.legal_principle: The Court would not consider on appeal an objection that was not made in the High Court and that required factual investigation.

predicates.civil_tax_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning a local body’s tax levy.
predicates.budget_objection_not_raised_below: The party did not raise its objection about the local body’s budget in the court below.
predicates.budget_objection_requires_fact_inquiry: Resolving the budget objection requires investigation of facts.

issues.definition: In a tax appeal, a budget objection is not considered when it was not raised below and resolving it requires factual investigation.

issues.legal_issue: A local body cannot sustain a building-permission fee without statutory authority for the levy, and a fee must be correlated with services rendered individually to the person charged.
material_facts: The local body demanded a fee for permission to construct factory and other buildings.
The governing law did not generally require permission to construct buildings, although it required permission for certain factories.
The local body provided no evidence of services rendered or intended to be rendered individually to the person charged, or of the cost of such services.
The fee was calculated as a percentage of the buildings’ capital value.
The local body relied on roads, drainage, lighting, and scrutiny of plans, but these were not shown to be services rendered individually to the person charged.
issues.conclusion: The permission fee was illegal. The asserted public functions did not establish an individual service relationship, and the fee’s calculation by reference to capital value showed no correlation with services.
issues.legal_principle: A fee is consideration for services and requires a correlation between the levy and services rendered to the person charged. Services must be rendered or intended to be rendered individually to that person; the general activities or statutory functions of a public body do not suffice. A levy also requires statutory authority. Section 131(2) did not apply where permission was not required, and section 217(2)(xvi) could not supply a permission requirement for other buildings in the absence of authority in the parent Act. The Court relied on Commissioner, Hindu Religious Endowments, Madras v. Shri Lakshmindar Thirtha Swamiar of Sri Shirur Mutt.

rule.if: civil_tax_appeal and building_permission_fee_charged and (no_statutory_authority_for_fee or no_statutory_permission_requirement) and no_individualized_service_correlation and fee_based_on_building_capital_value

predicates.civil_tax_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning a local body’s levy.
predicates.building_permission_fee_charged: A local body charged a person a fee in connection with permission to construct a building.
predicates.no_statutory_authority_for_fee: The governing law does not authorize the local body to impose the fee.
predicates.no_statutory_permission_requirement: The governing law does not require permission for the construction in question.
predicates.no_individualized_service_correlation: The local body has not shown a correlation between the fee and services rendered or intended to be rendered individually to the person charged.
predicates.fee_based_on_building_capital_value: The fee is calculated by reference to the capital value of the building rather than the cost of individualized services.

issues.definition: A building-permission fee is invalid when it lacks statutory authority or a statutory permission requirement and is not correlated with individualized services, particularly where it is based on building value.

issues.legal_issue: A fee charged upon applying for permission to construct a building cannot be upheld as a tax on buildings when liability does not depend on whether a building is constructed.
material_facts: The fee became payable when permission to construct was applied for.
The fee remained payable even if the proposed building was never constructed.
issues.conclusion: The fee could not be upheld as a tax on buildings because it was a levy on a proposed activity rather than on buildings.
issues.legal_principle: The nature of a levy depends on what triggers liability. A levy payable upon an application, independently of whether a building comes into existence, is imposed on the proposed activity and is not a tax on buildings.

rule.if: civil_tax_appeal and construction_permission_levy and fee_payable_on_application and liability_independent_of_completed_building

predicates.civil_tax_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning a local body’s levy.
predicates.construction_permission_levy: The challenged levy is imposed in connection with permission to construct a building.
predicates.fee_payable_on_application: The person becomes liable to pay the levy when applying for permission.
predicates.liability_independent_of_completed_build: The liability remains even if the proposed building is never constructed.

issues.definition: A levy connected with construction permission is not a building tax when it is payable on application regardless of whether a building is completed.
